messages.text: Bring the muon engineer and the project coordinator in and adapt the muon system envelopes for those setups, if chosen we will make an issue to update the baseline.

I’ll bring the muon engineer and coordinator together to propose candidate-specific muon envelopes. I’ll document the space changes and update the comparison drawings; the baseline update issue can follow once a layout is chosen.

The engineer and coordinator have agreed on concrete study envelopes for all six options. The iron-return, toroid and active-return layouts get larger hosts, with the return-coil space accounted for separately. The expanded endcaps stop at |z| = 10.9 m, leaving a 0.30 m gap before forward calorimetry; that gap still needs a service and support check.

The revised drawings now show all six candidate envelopes against the original baseline. They pass the coarse overlap checks, but a concern remains: the larger radial envelopes do not establish that end-return structures, chambers and services fit in the endcap space—particularly for MAG-04 and MAG-06. I’m keeping that limitation explicit in the PR.

The proposals are committed for PR #6. The candidate outer barrel radii are 7.50 m for MAG-02/03, 10.00 m for MAG-04, 9.00 m for MAG-05 and 8.85 m for MAG-06; MAG-01 retains the reference envelope. I’m updating the executive summary to make these space costs clear.

The muon engineer and coordinator adapted all six candidate envelopes in [PR #6](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/6), with explicit space budgets and updated r–z drawings.

**Remaining concern:** MAG-04/06 end-return structures and services still need a demonstrated fit within the proposed endcaps.

Envelope checks and CI passed. The baseline remains unchanged; no update issue was created, as requested pending layout selection.
